installation.note: bash is the default login shell on most Linux distributions

overview.summary: bash is a Unix shell and command language. It is the default shell on most Linux systems and supports scripting, job control, history, and many built-in commands. Invoking bash starts an interactive shell or runs a script.
when_to_use: Execute commands in a subshell with bash -c

syntax.description: Without SCRIPT, bash starts an interactive shell. With SCRIPT, it runs the script. Use -c to run a command string.

options.description: Run COMMAND as a single string (no script file)
options.use_case: One-liner or script passed as argument

options.description: Print commands and arguments as they are executed (debug)
Read commands but do not execute (syntax check)

related_commands.description: POSIX shell; often a link to dash or bash
Run script in current shell (source script.sh or . script.sh)
